auditor_statement: I audited the attempt-2 CPU prefreeze independently and adversarially, with explicit guard against rubber-stamping my own attempt-1 prescriptions. I recomputed every claimed hash, re-ran tamper and bypass attacks against the v2 config gate, attacked the new reference-checkpoint authentication with nine crafted-directory/forged-manifest/symlink variants, attacked enforce_machine_id with every protected ID plus malformed and coercion-trick inputs, independently re-derived the pythia parameter count analytically, verified the scorer join against genuine write_scores output and the GenerationSummary key surface, re-ran the full test and lint suites, verified commit hygiene and v1-artifact immutability at HEAD, and performed the requested fresh-eyes sweep over defect classes I did not examine in attempt 1. Every attempt-1 defect is genuinely and robustly fixed. The verdict is nevertheless no-go, because the fresh-eyes sweep found a forgeable evidence binding on the challenger side that meets the same P0 definition I applied in attempt 1. The identical gap existed in the v1 runner and I failed to flag it in attempt 1; that omission was mine and is recorded here rather than hidden.
go_criterion: zero P0 defects (P0 = leakage, forgeable receipt/binding, sealed-data access, denylist gap, silent fallback, authorization-flag escape)

defects.title: Challenger snapshot bytes are unbound: undetectable weight/config substitution channel into the adoption decision
defects.detail: The decision-critical candidate-v2 reference is now fully hash-authenticated, but the three challenger arms are not. The runner verifies only tokenizer.json against a pin; model.safetensors for pythia-70m-deduped, SmolLM2-135M, and SmolLM2-360M is neither hash-pinned in the frozen config nor verified after snapshot_download nor recorded into arm-result.json or result.json. huggingface_hub returns a cached snapshot for a pinned revision without re-hashing blob contents, so a pre-staged --cache-dir can substitute arbitrary challenger weights - including weights pre-exposed to the 725 selection rows, a direct leakage channel into a measured arm - while every receipt truthfully-looking claims the pinned revision produced the scores. No post-hoc independent verification from the evidence bundle is possible. Aggravating factors: (1) the v2 config pins config_json_sha256 and tokenizer_config_sha256 per arm, but the runner never checks either, so the frozen config advertises binding coverage that does not exist (the claimed-but-unenforced-binding defect class behind prior repository no-gos); config.json defines the architecture being measured and is loaded unverified by AutoModelForCausalLM. (2) AGENTS.md experiment discipline requires each run to record 'base checkpoint and tokenizer revisions and hashes'; challenger checkpoint hashes are recorded nowhere. (3) The accepted mobile_qwen05b_matched lane pinned and verified its entire baseline snapshot per file plus safetensors byte length, so the repository standard for exactly this lane class already includes full snapshot binding; v2 regresses from it. Mitigations honestly noted: the frozen compute plan is one fresh exact-ID H200 whose fresh hub download is TLS-delivered and content-addressed by etag, the parameter-count assertion and tokenizer pin bound gross substitutions, and exploitation requires deliberate operator staging. Those mitigations do not make substitution detectable from the receipts, which is the repository's operative standard (closure-cell, dependency-injection, and unproven-checkpoint-provenance rejections all involved operator-malice channels).
defects.classification_basis: forgeable receipt/binding and leakage per the frozen P0 definition; consistent with the attempt-1 P0-1 standard (an unauthenticated input whose substitution the evidence cannot detect)
defects.attempt_1_omission: the identical gap existed in the v1 runner; the attempt-1 audit did not flag it. This finding comes from the explicitly requested fresh-eyes sweep (evidence-bundle completeness, dependency-identity binding), not from a moved goalpost: the standard cited (AGENTS.md hash-recording requirement; qwen-lane full-snapshot pinning) predates both audits.
defects.required_minimal_correction: In a successor config and runner revision: (a) pin per-arm SHA-256 for model.safetensors (available without weight downloads via read-only Hugging Face metadata: files_metadata LFS sha256) plus config.json, tokenizer_config.json, and generation_config.json (or its pinned absence, as for pythia-70m-deduped at the pinned revision); (b) verify every downloaded snapshot file the loader can read against those pins after snapshot_download, aborting on mismatch or on unexpected extra model-affecting files; (c) record the verified per-file hashes into arm-result.json and result.json; (d) either enforce or remove the currently unenforced config_json_sha256/tokenizer_config_sha256 pins so the config claims exactly what the code checks.

defects.title: Frozen generation_config_overrides never applied or asserted; decoding fields inherit from an unverified snapshot file
defects.detail: evaluation.generation_config_overrides freezes do_sample/num_beams/repetition_penalty/no_repeat_ngram_size/length_penalty/temperature/top_k/top_p, but _generate_selection passes only do_sample, max_new_tokens, eos_token_id, pad_token_id, and use_cache to model.generate. All remaining decoding fields default from the snapshot's generation_config.json, which is downloaded but neither pinned nor verified; repetition_penalty and no_repeat_ngram_size alter greedy argmax selection. Honest-path check performed read-only at the pinned revisions: pythia-70m-deduped has no generation_config.json (404) and both SmolLM2 files contain only bos/eos IDs, so the honest path is exactly greedy as frozen. The defect is that an unverified file can influence decision-affecting decoding and that the config binds overrides the code does not enforce. Correction folds into P0-3: pin/verify generation_config.json (or its absence) and pass the frozen overrides explicitly to model.generate.

defects.title: Preregistered measured-failure semantics for fits are unreachable; challenger generation has no OOM handling
defects.detail: The config's learning_rate_screen_rule states a fit that fails to complete can never win and two failed fits make the arm a measured failure, and evaluation.measured_failures counts OOMs as failures. In the runner, every fit is recorded completed=True and any training or generation exception (non-finite loss, OOM) propagates and aborts the entire run; select_learning_rate's failed-fit branch is dead code on the production path. Unlike generate_manifest (which records per-batch OOMs as measured generation failures), _generate_selection has no OutOfMemoryError handling. This fails closed - a partial run leaves no result.json and cannot masquerade as complete (verified: result.json with status 'completed' is written once, at the end) - but it contradicts the preregistered contract text and can burn the 6-hour budget on a single recoverable fault. Correction: implement per-fit failure capture consistent with the frozen rule, or amend the successor config text to state that any fit failure terminates the run as an infrastructure failure.

defects.title: No torch.manual_seed or deterministic-algorithms binding
defects.detail: Seed 17 governs only data presentation order. No stochastic modules exist on the honest path (pinned pythia config has no dropout fields, SmolLM2 attention_dropout is 0.0, greedy decoding, no weight init), so runs are deterministic modulo CUDA kernel nondeterminism, but the receipts' 'seed 17' claim is narrower than a reader might assume. Informational.

defects.detail: torch/transformers/tokenizers versions are not recorded in result.json; the repository convention delegates environment binding to the launch tooling's environment.json. Acceptable by convention; noted for evidence-bundle completeness.

defects.title: Residual TOCTOU window between reference verification and file reads

Exploiting the remainder requires concurrent write access on the remote host during the run. Informational.

what_this_no_go_means: Attempt 2 fully and robustly repairs every attempt-1 defect; nothing in this receipt reopens those findings. The single blocking defect is the unbound challenger snapshot evidence (P0-3). No GPU, CUDA, JarvisLabs resource, weight download, training, or official-961 access is authorized. The required corrections are exact and small; a successor freeze that pins, verifies, and records challenger snapshot file hashes (and aligns the claimed bindings and decoding overrides with enforced code) plus a fresh independent audit is the path to launch.
required_minimal_corrections: Pin per-arm snapshot file hashes (model.safetensors via read-only HF LFS metadata; config.json; tokenizer_config.json; generation_config.json or its recorded absence) in the successor config; verify each after snapshot_download; record verified hashes into arm-result.json and result.json.
Enforce or remove the currently unenforced config_json_sha256 / tokenizer_config_sha256 pins so the frozen config claims exactly what the runner checks.
Pass the frozen generation_config_overrides explicitly to model.generate (or construct an explicit GenerationConfig) so no unverified snapshot file can influence decoding.
Optional but recommended (P2-B): implement the preregistered per-fit measured-failure semantics or amend the contract text to declare any fit failure a run-terminating infrastructure failure.
